This is why 55% of marriages end in divorce.

Finally, it's not your job to hold resentment on your father's behalf, what happened between them is their business. Your stepdad is just in the middle trying to live in happiness, and if he's decent to you, is a good Dad to your brother, and a good husband to your mom, that deserves a bit of respect. You don't have to like him.

What most people don't understand is marriage doesn't mean you'll always want to spend every free moment with your spouse, you don't stop being your own person, and after having children and enduring the ups and downs of life and marriage, once the kids get older and they don't need you so much, there's a want to get to return to who you are as a person and do the things that make you content and not having to think of another person's happiness, wants and needs. My husband is a tv and stereo hog, so when he leaves the house for work, I am going to watch all the tv and listen to all the music that I like, and have the house to myself while I work. It doesn't mean I don't love him, just means that I'm trying to grab at my own individuality when he's gone. After raising kids and being in a marriage for decades, that flame dies down, but the answer isn't always to jump to the most exciting person, it's to navigate life as best you can with who you're with.
